newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Eramet shares hit by nickel mine row.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eramet shares hit by nickel mine row.

text.p: Shares in France's Eramet SA, the world's third-biggest nickel producer, fell on Monday after the government said it had started moves to withdraw a nickel mining licence for Koniambo in New Caledonia.

The French government, claiming Eramet had not exploited the mine since 1975, wants to hand the concession to local Kanak interests on the South Pacific island so that the ore can be used in a new nickel smelter.
The smelter project is part of a deal to appease Kanaks ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence among the 197,000 people on the island, 18,000 kms (11,200 miles) from mainland France.
Shares in Eramet, which owns the exploitation rights and is 55 percent owned by the state, closed 11.76 percent down at 270 francs.

The Industry Ministry said that a 1954 mining decree allowed expropriation if the Koniambo mine was not exploited for more than 10 years. It said it had started the administrative procedure to withdraw the mining lincence.
"The government will see to it that the patrimonial interests of Eramet will not be hurt," the ministry said.

In a statement, Eramet said it would use all legal means in its possession to prevent the disappropriation, which it said would cause it "considerable prejudice" and would affect its financial outlook.

The company said it believed that under current laws and regulations in New Caledonia such a decision could not be justified. It said its Societe Le Nickel (SLN) had been operating the mine for more than a century and planned to increase production.
A spokesman for Eramet said the company was "surprised" by the government decision and "did not understand" the motives.
He confirmed the mine had not been used since 1975.
A government official said the state had taken the decision about the Koniambo expropriation after asset swap talks between SLN and Kanak Societe Miniere du Sud Pacifique (SMSP) failed.
"The companies could not agree amongst each other because the SMSP wanted a deal with immediate effect," he said.
The government plans to start talks over compensation.

Eramet, which only has mines on New Caledonia, planned to start Koniambo again in 2008 and said it would be at full capacity in 2010. "Koniambo represents 50 percent of our future nickel ore needs," the spokesman said.

Eramet plans to produce 60,000 to 65,000 tonnes of nickel per year after 2000 and any compensation for Koniambo would need to provide ore sufficient for the production of 30,000 to 35,000 tonnes per year.

On January 30, the French government and officials of the two main political parties of the French South Pacific island of New Caledonia agreed to re-allocate mining reserves within the territory so that local Kanak independence groups could go ahead with plans to build a nickel plant in the north.
